transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-18
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Ortiz (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Meera Sundaram (LatticeWard Head of MLOps), Carlos Ruiz (CTO), Priya Nandakumar (Platform Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- LatticeWard is evaluating Dedicated for low-latency inference with strict tenant isolation and burst allowances.
- Primary constraints: per-tenant quotas, billing/chargeback, VPC-only private control plane, and KMS-backed key rotation.
- Next step: pricing + pilot runbook + sample trace exchange.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Jamie (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, and then maybe Samir will walk through the topology options.
[00:08] Meera (LatticeWard): Hi, thanks. We have about 45 minutes — Carlos and Priya on the line as well. We mainly want to understand how Redwood Dedicated would handle our tenant throttling and burst shaping.
[00:18] Samir (Redwood): Great, quick ack. I'll start high-level then dive into prewarm/hotpool behavior. So at a top level Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, you can do tenant segmentation by node pools or by lightweight sharding via runtime routing.
[00:31] Carlos (LatticeWard): When you say 'sharding'—is that per-tenant pinned node or shared multi-tenant with quotas? We have a mix, some tenants need soft isolation, others require strict isolation for compliance.
[00:44] Samir (Redwood): Both are possible. We support fully segregated node assignment (tenant fencing) — that's literal dedicated GPU nodes per customer-tenant — and we also support logical quotas on shared pools. The tradeoff: cost and cold-start behavior.
[00:58] Priya (LatticeWard): Can you talk about warm pools? Our spike pattern is 10x baseline for 20-30 minutes, 3-4 times a week. We need quick ramp up without huge token cost.
[01:12] Samir (Redwood): Yes. We have hot-pool or prewarm lanes. Prewarm keeps model state and KV cache ready; hot-pool is smaller and can spin routes into larger pools quickly. In practice you'll configure a base reserved capacity plus a burst allowance backed by autoscaling. We also have burst gating rules so tenanted traffic doesn’t overwhelm a shared pool.
[01:30] Meera: When you say KV cache ready — sometimes transcripts say KV cash — but sorry — we mean the attention cache for prompt prefix reuse. 
[01:36] Jamie: (laughs) Yeah, the autosub transcriber gets creative.
[01:40] [02:05] Carlos: How predictable is latency during a spike if the hot-pool is exhausted? Do you fall back to a hosted variant or queuing?
[02:12] Samir: We have a few fallback mechanisms — you can choose fallback to a lighter-parameter model variant hosted in another region, or to queue and return a retry-after. For latency-sensitive features we typically recommend a small reserved tail with burst allowance plus model variant fallback.
[02:28] Meera: For compliance tenants we might prefer on-prem or VPC private deployment. Does Redwood Private support the same hot-pool semantics?
[02:36] Samir: Yes, Private supports identical runtime semantics; the difference is control plane and network. On-prem is more manual ops, but the runtime's prewarm/hotpool features are the same.
[02:47] Priya: Any differences in KMS integration? We use an HSM provider with key rotation requirements.
[02:54] Jamie: We integrate with customer-managed KMS in Dedicated via our VPC options, and Private supports HSM too. We'll share the KMS integration doc — there's a short checklist for rotation windows and envelope encryption.
[03:07] [03:35] Meera: Ok, on tenant quota shaping — we want strict per-tenant concurrency and a soft token cap that gets throttled during system-wide spikes. How do you model that?
[03:45] Samir: You can configure per-tenant rate limits (req/sec) and token budgets over rolling windows. On burst, we apply shaping policies: guaranteed baseline, best-effort burst, and a circuit-breaker for aggressive tenants. Also we expose token-level telemetry so you can do chargeback.
[04:01] Carlos: Does that token telemetry map to the console billing? We need per-tenant cost attribution.
[04:06] Jamie: Yes, Console has per-route and per-token breakdowns; you can surface tenant tags and export to your billing system. We'll show you the tagging pattern in the pilot.
[04:18] [05:10] Priya: What about preemption? If another high-priority workload needs the node, do you preempt tenant VMs or do you spill to other pools?
[05:20] Samir: We don't do noisy-preempt on customer reserved pools; instead you can configure priority classes. For shared pools we will evict best-effort workers first. For Dedicated reserved nodes, preemption is a customer config; generally we avoid live preemptions without agreement.
[05:34] Meera: That matters. Our legal says no preemption for certain customers.
[05:38] Samir: Noted. We can model a 'gold' tenant class pinned to dedicated nodes.
[05:44] [06:15] Carlos: Let's talk numbers—if we reserve 8 A100-equivalent GPUs, what throughput/user latency can we expect for our shortest prompts?
[06:25] Samir: Depends on model and quantization. For a typical 13B open model with q4 quantization, you might see ~60-80 tokens per GPU-second in steady state with low-latency tails if batching is tuned. For 8-GPU reserve you can derive concurrency targets; we'll run benchmarks with your prompt shapes in the pilot.
[06:47] Meera: We do some 70-200 token prompts mostly. Is continuous batching an issue for percentiles?
[06:53] Samir: Continuous batching helps throughput but can add tail latency for P99 if batch windows are long; we tune low-latency workloads with smaller batch windows and smarter kernel selection. We'll show latency-by-tuning knobs in the pilot.
[07:09] [07:50] Priya: Regarding network — do we need a dedicated VPC peering tunnel for Dedicated? We use strict egress rules.
[07:58] Jamie: For Dedicated we support customer VPC peering or PrivateLink. You can lock down egress, and we support IP allowlists and SAML-based SSO for the console.
[08:12] Meera: Auditing — can we get daily audit logs for model invocations?
[08:18] Samir: Yes, invocation logs, token-level metrics, and KV cache heatmaps are available; retention is configurable. For compliance we'll enable immutable audit export to your storage.
[08:30] [09:00] Carlos: Security review — we need SOC2 Type II evidence and a penetration test report. Do you provide that?
[09:06] Jamie: Yes, we'll share our SOC2 pack and recent pentest summary. For Private deployments we can agree to additional audits under the enterprise contract. Link will be in the follow-up.
[09:18] [10:00] Meera: One of our concerns is cost predictability — burst charges can be surprising. How do you model burst billing vs. reserved?
[10:08] Jamie: Pricing model has two parts: reserved monthly commitment (committed GPUs) and overage/burst at a per-GPU-minute rate. We provide a burst smoothing option with a capped per-day overage to limit surprises. We'll include examples in the pricing matrix.
[10:24] Priya: Do you support unit-based chargeback? e.g., per-tenant token rates?
[10:29] Jamie: Console exports per-tenant token usage and you can ingest to your billing pipeline. We also provide a CSV with cost allocation.
[10:36] [12:05] Samir: Small demo point — our runtime supports prefix/KV caching that reduces tokens spent on repeated system prompts. If your features reuse the same system context, you see big savings.
[12:21] Meera: Good. We'll provide a sample set where we see repeated context.
[12:28] [13:00] Carlos: Regarding pilot success criteria — we want P95 < 200ms for the short prompts, no tenant bleed during 10x spikes, and clear cost attribution. Is that achievable?
[13:12] Samir: Achievable with the right config. P95 depends on model and prewarm sizing; we'll size the pilot tail accordingly. We'll instrument the pilot with synthetic and real traffic.
[13:25] Meera: How long is the pilot typically?
[13:28] Jamie: We typically do a 48–72 hour controlled pilot for surge tests, then a 2-week proof-of-load for production validation. For billing you'd get a pilot invoice at reduced rate or credit depending on the commercial offer.
[13:40] [15:00] Priya: Onboarding — what telemetry hooks do you need? We can forward traces, and we use OpenTelemetry today.
[15:08] Samir: We accept OTLP spans and metrics. We'll need request IDs and tenant tags surfaced in headers. We'll share the minimal schema.
[15:22] Meera: About the fallback model you mentioned, if the reserved pool is out we fallback to hosted lighter models — any data residency issues there?
[15:32] Jamie: Good callout. We only fallback to variants that match customer data residency constraints; if you require strict on-prem processing we will not fallback to hosted without explicit consent.
[15:45] [17:10] Carlos: Are there network egress implications for fallback? If we fallback to a hosted variant in a different region will latency be impacted?
[17:18] Samir: Yes, fallback region selection matters for latency. We prefer same-region fallback when available; otherwise you get added RTT. We'll test fallback paths in the pilot.
[17:30] [19:00] Meera: Can you walk briefly through the pilot instrumentation and what dashboards we'll get?
[19:10] Samir: We provide a pilot dashboard with per-tenant qps, token consumption, latency percentiles, KV cache hit rates, and a burst event timeline. We'll give you read-only access and an export endpoint for raw telemetry.
[19:25] Priya: For token conservation, you mentioned quantization recommendations — are those automatic?
[19:32] Samir: Redwood Optimize suggests quantization and model variants based on your workload; recommendations are advisory and we run validation to check quality regressions.
[19:45] [21:10] Carlos: Commercial — if we sign annual reserved capacity, are burst allowances included or extra?
[21:18] Jamie: Burst allowances are optional add-ons. Typically customers buy a baseline reserve and purchase a burst pool which is cheaper than pure on-demand but billable when used. We can model a buffer in the contract to cap daily overages.
[21:30] Meera: For legal, we need an SLA for p999 latency or uptime?
[21:36] Jamie: We provide SLA for uptime and best-effort latency SLOs for Dedicated. For stricter latency guarantees we can discuss higher-tier SLA with additional engineering support.
[21:50] [23:00] Priya: Are model rollouts supported? We want to A/B two variants and canary to 5% of traffic.
[23:08] Samir: Yes, rollout controls support canary, A/B and automatic rollback on eval regressions. You can pin tenants to versions.
[23:20] Meera: That's important. We need pinned versions per-tenant.
[23:24] Samir: Supported.
[23:30] [25:00] Carlos: Anything else on the compliance side, like log immutability or certified key storage?
[25:08] Jamie: We support immutable export and customer-managed key stores. For highly regulated customers we do on-site audits as part of Private deals.
[25:20] Meera: Ok. To recap, we'll get pricing, KMS/security pack, and a pilot plan. Jamie will own pricing and Samir will own the pilot runbook. We'll share traffic traces.
[25:40] Jamie: Correct. I'll attach a pricing matrix and a short checklist for telemetry. Samir will follow with the runbook and instrumentation schema.
[25:52] [27:00] Meera: One more question — how do you protect against tenant bypassing quotas with synthetic traffic? We need throttles at multiple layers.
[27:10] Samir: We have request validation, rate-limits at the ingress proxy, and token-budgets enforced server-side. You can add an additional gateway layer with custom rules if needed.
[27:22] [30:00] Priya: Are there limits on model quantization — do you support int8 for certain architectures?
[30:06] Samir: We support q4/q8-like quant options depending on the model family and we test quality impact. Some architectures don't work well with aggressive quant.
[30:20] Meera: We'll include quality thresholds in the pilot.
[30:24] [33:00] Carlos: Benchmarks — can you run an initial dry-run with synthetic 10x spikes to validate shaping?
[33:09] Samir: Yes, our pilot includes synthetic spike tests and real traffic validation. We'll define the scenarios in the runbook.
[33:26] [35:00] Jamie: Ok last part — schedule and next steps. We aim to run the pilot week of 2027-08-30. Pricing and docs by 2027-08-20. Any objections?
[35:12] Meera: No objections. Sounds good.
[35:18] Carlos: Agreed.
[35:22] Priya: Agreed.
[35:30] [37:00] Jamie: Great. I'll follow up with the pricing deck and the SOC2 link. Samir will send the pilot runbook and an instrumentation schema.
[37:15] Meera: One last operational ask — can you include an example of tenant tag propagation in headers? That'll help our billing pipeline.
[37:23] Samir: Yes will include header examples and sample OTLP mapping.
[37:30] [38:40] Jamie: Alright thanks everyone. We'll track action items in the CRM and follow up.
[38:50] Meera: Thanks, bye.
[38:53] Carlos: Thanks all.
[38:55] Priya: Thanks, bye.
